provenance.quote: Shall a retailers' sales tax in the amount of one percent (1.00%) be levied in the City of Andale, Kansas, to take effect April 1, 2027, or as soon thereafter as such tax may be levied by the Kansas Department of Revenue, with revenue from such tax used for the purposes of providing mill levy support, assistance in establishing a General Fund Stabilization Reserve, and for Parks, Sidewalks, Roads and other General Government Purposes, including payment of debt service on financings issued for such purposes; and provided that such retailers' sales tax shall expire on the date ten years after it is first levied, all pursuant to K.S.A 12-187, et seq., as amended?

contests.title: Valley Center — Public safety sales tax

provenance.quote: Shall the City of Valley Center, Kansas, be authorized to impose a one percent (1%) Citywide retailers' sales tax, the revenue from which will be used to enhance public safety services, including fire and police operations, capital improvements, equipment, and maintenance within the City and all improvements related thereto (“Public Safety Purposes”), including payment of debt service on financings issued for Public Safety Purposes, with the collection of such sales tax to commence on April 1, 2027, or as soon thereafter as permitted by law, and continue in effect until it is repealed by the Governing Body; all pursuant to the provisions of K.S.A. 12‑187 et seq., as amended?

contests.title: Wichita USD 259 — Proposition 1: School improvement bonds

provenance.quote: Shall Unified School District No. 259, Sedgwick County, Kansas (Wichita) (the “District”), issue general obligation bonds in an amount not to exceed $407,100,000, to pay the costs to make improvements in the District, including the following: Construct, furnish and equip a new Trades Future Ready Center; Construct, furnish, equip: HVAC and air quality improvements at five high schools, eleven middle schools, and Manufacturing FRC; Vehicle and pedestrian improvements at existing District facilities, including Isely K-8 Academy, Seltzer Elementary School and Christa McAuliffe K-8 Academy; Preservation improvements at: North High School; East High School; Rebuild, renovate, construct, furnish, and/or equip for: Truesdell Middle School; Black Elementary School; McLean Magnet Elementary School; Chisholm Trail Elementary School into a new K–8 facility; Cessna Elementary School including a middle school addition; Construct, furnish, renovate and equip other necessary building, technology, efficiency, and utility improvements at District facilities from remaining proceeds of the bonds; and pay fees, costs and expenses incidental thereto; all pursuant to the provisions of K.S.A. 10‑101 et seq., K.S.A. 25‑2018(f), K.S.A. 72‑5457, and K.S.A. 72‑5458 et seq.?

contests.title: Wichita USD 259 — Proposition 2: School improvement bonds

provenance.quote: Shall Unified School District No. 259, Sedgwick County, Kansas (Wichita) (the “District”), issue general obligation bonds in an amount not to exceed $207,900,000, to pay the costs to make improvements in the District, including the following: Upgrade, remodel, rebuild, renovate, furnish, equip, and/or construct improvements to: repurpose the existing Hadley facility to serve as the new Horace Mann Dual Language K-8 Magnet; repurpose the existing Horace Mann facility to serve as the new Irving Elementary School; repurpose the existing OK Elementary School to serve as a new early childhood center; Preservation improvements at high schools aged 50 years and older; Construct, furnish and equip improvements to career and technical education facilities at South, Northwest, Heights, and West High Schools, auditorium improvements at Heights High School, and parking improvements at West High School; Rebuild, renovate, furnish, equip, and/or construct improvements to: Rebuild a new Coleman Middle School, renovate the existing school to repurpose for alternative programs; Adams Elementary School; Construct, furnish, renovate and equip other necessary building, technology, efficiency, and utility improvements at District facilities from remaining proceeds of the bonds; and pay fees, costs and expenses incidental thereto; all pursuant to the provisions of K.S.A. 10‑101 et seq., K.S.A. 25‑2018(f), K.S.A. 72‑5457, and K.S.A. 72‑5458 et seq.?

provenance.sourceOrg: Reno County Clerk and Election Officer
provenance.quote: Shall Unified School District No. 308, Reno County, Kansas (Hutchinson), issue general obligation bonds in an amount not to exceed $36,000,000, to pay the costs to construct, furnish and equip: (a) improvements and renovations to the District’s facilities, including HVAC, roofs, safety and security, storm shelter, restrooms and playground improvements; and (b) all necessary improvements related thereto (the “Project”), and pay costs of issuance and interest on the Bonds during construction of the Project, all pursuant to the provisions of K.S.A. 10-101 et seq., K.S.A. 25-2018(f), K.S.A. 72-5457, and K.S.A. 72-5458 et seq.?

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes a 1% city sales tax for ten years, starting April 1, 2027, or as soon afterward as the law allows. Money could support property-tax funding needs, a general-fund reserve, parks, sidewalks, roads, other general city purposes and debt payments for those purposes.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize the 1% sales tax for these ten years and purposes.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize this sales tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes a 1% city sales tax for police and fire operations, public-safety equipment, capital improvements, maintenance and debt payments for those purposes. Collection would start April 1, 2027, or as soon afterward as the law allows, and continue until the city repeals the tax.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize the 1% sales tax for public safety.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize this sales tax.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Wichita school district to borrow up to $407.1 million through general-obligation bonds for school buildings, a trades training center, air quality, access, technology and related costs.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize up to $407.1 million in bonds for this proposition’s school improvements.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize the bonds in this proposition.

parts.label: Trades training center
parts.what: Build, furnish and equip a new Trades Future Ready Center.

parts.label: Air quality and access
parts.what: Improve heating, cooling and air quality at five high schools, eleven middle schools and the Manufacturing Future Ready Center. Improve vehicle and pedestrian access at district facilities, including Isely K-8, Seltzer Elementary and Christa McAuliffe K-8.

parts.label: Preservation and school rebuilding
parts.what: Preserve North and East high schools. Rebuild or renovate Truesdell Middle, Black Elementary and McLean Magnet Elementary; make Chisholm Trail a K-8 facility; and add middle-school space at Cessna Elementary.

parts.label: Remaining proceeds and financing costs
parts.what: Use remaining bond proceeds for other necessary building, technology, efficiency and utility improvements, and pay related fees, costs and expenses.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Wichita school district to borrow up to $207.9 million through general-obligation bonds for school reuse and rebuilding, older high schools, career and technical education facilities, and related improvements and costs.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize up to $207.9 million in bonds for this proposition’s school improvements.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize the bonds in this proposition.

parts.label: Reuse school facilities
parts.what: Adapt Hadley for the Horace Mann Dual Language K-8 Magnet; adapt the existing Horace Mann building for Irving Elementary; and turn OK Elementary into an early childhood center.

parts.label: High-school improvements
parts.what: Preserve high schools at least 50 years old. Improve career and technical education facilities at South, Northwest, Heights and West; the auditorium at Heights; and parking at West.

parts.label: Coleman and Adams schools
parts.what: Build a new Coleman Middle School and renovate the current building for alternative programs. Rebuild, renovate or otherwise improve Adams Elementary.

parts.label: Remaining proceeds and financing costs
parts.what: Use remaining bond proceeds for other necessary building, technology, efficiency and utility improvements, and pay related fees, costs and expenses.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows the school district to borrow up to $36 million through general-obligation bonds for building improvements, including heating and cooling, roofs, safety and security, a storm shelter, restrooms and playgrounds. It also allows related improvements, bond-issuance costs and interest during construction.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize up to $36 million in bonds for these school improvements and related costs.
